title: Source-root naming refused 'named-root binding requires an active host session' for a root session with a live native claim
outcome: A root session holding a live claim under turn-gated control OFF can name its worktree even after its Engram control session was left exited. A named_root_binding_refused answer flags the session's still-held token for a re-bind, and naming again re-binds it and binds the named root. Any refusal a re-bind does not cure states which precondition failed and the supported remedy.
acceptance: Which of the two refusal branches in Engram control_runtime.rs:107-113 failed for session-12325 is established from evidence (the control session phase, and the claim's actor session against the bind's session).

Under turn-gated control OFF, when Engram refuses named_root_bind with named_root_binding_refused while the session still holds the refused routing token, TermAl flags that token rebind_required in the same save; a test shows that naming the same root again then re-binds the session through the flagged-token naming bind and binds the named root.

Every named_root_binding_refused answer that this re-bind does not cure (turn-gated control ON, or a session that no longer holds the refused token) keeps today's state handling, and its 409 names the failed precondition and the supported remedy; a test covers such a refusal and its message.
Engram::Fable confirms from Engram's code, recorded on this item, that a session_bind made while the project's gated control is OFF cures both refusal branches and grants no gated authority.
The change is reviewed and gated under the standing rule.
